_comment: mwcceppc (GameCube PowerPC) codegen lever catalogue. One lever per line; read it with tools/levers.py, not by hand-parsing. This is a DISTILLED INDEX, not the evidence - `source` points at where each was actually derived. Schema is deliberately identical to tangosdev/sm64ds-decomp notes/levers.jsonl so the two are readable by the same tool across a sibling checkout; that catalogue covers mwccarm/NDS and this one covers mwcceppc/GameCube. Fields: arch = ISAs the mechanism is known or believed to work on; compiler_version = the mwcceppc versions it was established on, because GC/1.x and GC/2.x+ differ materially; confidence = proven (reproduced a byte-match) or probable.

symptom: every instruction matches but the whole function is shifted: stwu r1,-N(r1) reserves less than the target and every stack displacement is off by a constant
lever: the original produced more intermediate values here. GC/1.x never reclaims a stack slot, so anything that failed to win a register still costs frame even when its code was optimized away entirely. Find the inline call or longer expression chain that creates the missing temporaries; do NOT paper over it with a dummy local, that is a fakematch
note: the mwccarm catalogue's `volatile-local-stack-slot` is the sibling of this, but the mechanism differs: mwccarm DOES reclaim and needs volatile to pin a slot, whereas GC/1.x never reclaims at all. MEASURED REFINEMENT: frames carry 4 bytes of alignment padding, so one added 4-byte temporary is absorbed and does not move the frame at all. A +8 delta therefore means TWO more intermediate values, not one - do not go looking for a single missing local
tooling: tools/stack-frame-diff.py finds every instance tree-wide; identifying what occupies a given frame needs a compiler-state dumper
source: sms:tools/stack-frame-diff.py, proven on control__14TMapObjGeneralFv and THPPlayerInit
diagnosis: get a per-frame breakdown for the function and for a SIBLING that already matches, then compare them. Frames decompose into linkage / arguments / temps / saved registers / padding, and the deficit is in exactly one of those. Rule out the cheap explanations first: (a) extra callee-saved registers cannot be it if the function is frame-only, because saving another register adds stw/lwz instructions and would change the length - check the prologue bytes directly; (b) by-value class parameters do not home to the stack on mwcceppc, unlike mwccarm. What is left is compiler temporaries, one per intermediate value, which are created by inlined calls. MEASURED on TTelesaSlot::getSlotResult (PR #134): adding a named scalar local does NOTHING - five variants (int temp, float temp, both, temp on the first call, pointer walk) all produced byte-identical code AND an unchanged frame, because a scalar that is used gets a register and costs no stack. What moves the frame is an object that CANNOT win a register: a local array or a double. So the question is never 'which local is missing' but 'which non-register-allocatable object did the original have'
worked_example: the receiveMessage(THitActor*,u32) cluster: 9 overrides across 8 files sit at 0x20 and want 0x28, with byte-identical frame composition (arg 12 / linkage 8 / temp 4 / padding 4 / saved 4). Verified from the raw prologues that target and ours both save only r31 and are the same length, so the target's extra 8 bytes are two more temporaries that generate no code. Still unsolved; whoever cracks one likely gets all nine

symptom: a call is a bl in your build where the target inlined it, or the reverse; or the linker map wants a weak out-of-line copy of an inline function that you never emit
lever: MWCC gates inlining on STATEMENT COUNT, not code size. CInline_IsSmallFunction refuses anything over 15 statements outright. Past that the budget is per nesting pass: pass 0 (written directly in the function's own source) unlimited, pass 1 limit 10, pass 2 limit 7, pass 3 limit 3, pass 4 never runs. A call appearing as an ARGUMENT to another call counts one pass deeper. To make MWCC emit a weak out-of-line copy, arrange for at least one call to FAIL to inline
note: definition order does NOT gate inlining on GC/1.2.5 - a callee defined later still inlines. The widely repeated 'define before use' rule is false for this compiler
tooling: a compiler-state dumper reports the accept/refuse reason and callee statement counts
source: sms: getCurBckAnmPtr emitted at the map's exact size by collapsing setBckAnm from 15 to <=10 statements

symptom: a helper inlines at its top-level call site but stays a bl one layer deeper, truncating an inline chain you need
lever: collapse statements to get the function under the budget for the pass it is called at - an if/else folded into a ternary, or a declaration merged with its initialiser, each remove a statement. 15 is the hard gate; 10 is what matters at pass 1

symptom: __vt__ for a class lands in the wrong translation unit, taking its weak inline-virtual bodies and @NN@ adjustor thunks with it
lever: MWCC emits the vtable in the TU that defines the class's first non-inline, non-pure virtual in DECLARATION order. Move that declaration to change which TU owns the vtable. Reordering an OVERRIDE is layout-safe because the base fixes the slot; the destructor is also safe to move, MWCC pins it to its own slot
source: sms:include/MoveBG/MapObjGeneral.hpp, initMapObj promoted to first virtual

symptom: functions are all present and matching but sit in the wrong order in .text relative to the linker map
lever: with -inline deferred, .text emission order is the REVERSE of definition order in the source. Reorder the definitions, not the declarations
tooling: tools/validate-symbol-order.py (reverse_fn_order: True); tools/check-changed-symbol-order.py gates it in CI

symptom: you have declared a member virtual, but the linker map lists that symbol as UNUSED
lever: that combination is impossible: a virtual's address lives in a vtable, so mwld can never prove it unreachable and can never strip it. If the map says UNUSED, the original was not virtual - fix the declaration
note: checked across 2883 virtual declarations against 5134 UNUSED entries in mario.MAP: zero conflicts, so the invariant holds and is cheap to assert in CI

symptom: the function is byte-identical except that some values were coloured into different registers - same opcodes, same immediates, same structure
lever: recognise it and move on. MWCC's allocator is non-local: the colour a temp gets depends on whole-function register pressure, not the local statement, so there is no source construct that reliably forces a specific register. Changing the SHAPE of the computation (adding or removing a temporary) nudges pressure and is the only lever, but it is a shove not a dial
note: cross-checked against tangosdev/sm64ds-decomp, which reports the same wall on mwccarm and calls it the dominant blocker there. On SMS it is rare - only 20 of 2190 failing functions are pure register permutation - so unlike the ARM title this is NOT where our remaining work sits
tooling: tools/stack-frame-diff.py reports a `regperm` bucket; a compiler-state dumper (cadmic/mwcc-debugger) shows the allocator's priority list and coalescing state, which is the only way to see why a colour was chosen
source: sms: 20 cases measured 2026-08-22; mechanism per sm64ds notes/mwccarm-codegen.md section 2

symptom: Every instruction matches but many load/store displacements or addi immediates are off by one uniform amount, making it look like a struct member-offset shift / wrong header.
lever: Check the base register's provenance before believing a layout story. MWCC addresses statics and string literals as `lis rX,sym@ha` + `addi rD,rX,sym@l`, so a DATA offset occupies exactly the instruction field a struct displacement uses. If the base descends from a lis, the difference is data-pool ordering and the header is fine.
diagnosis: Disassemble and trace the base register. Then compare the two objects' .data symbol tables directly (`objdump -t`): if your first data symbol sits at a lower offset than the target's, your pool is missing bytes at the front.
worked_example: src/System/RenderModeObj.cpp: 4 functions differed by a uniform +40. GXRenderModeObj was suspected and is in fact correct (0x3C). Retail's .data begins with three dead compiler-generated constants -- @1431 {1.0f,1.0f,1.0f}, @1411 {1.0f,1.0f,1.0f}, @1210 {0,2,1,3} as u32 -- totalling 0x28 before SMSAASamplePattern_non; ours began with the array. Emitting 40 bytes of equivalent data at the head of .data made .data byte-identical and took the unit from 1 to 2 matched functions with every remaining difference reduced to stack frames. Project-wide this pattern accounted for 38 of 41 apparent 'member offset' shifts.
note: Supplying padding statics PROVES the diagnosis but must never ship -- it is compiler-fitting with no meaning. The real fix is reconstructing the source construct that produced the constants. Note the emission-order difference: named file-scope statics emit in DEFINITION order, while anonymous @NNNN constants emit in REVERSE creation order (@1210 created first appears last).
source: doldecomp/sms, measured 2026-08-23 across all 405 structural functions

symptom: a function is within a few instructions of the target with the frame already correct -- one operation, one condition, or one register assignment differs
lever: MWCC emits different code for semantically identical source spellings. When a function is close, the fix is usually a RESPELLING, not new logic. The families worth sweeping, safest first: bool (x / x != 0 / x != FALSE / x == TRUE), compare (comparison aliases of the same test), return (direct TRUE/FALSE vs a variable), decl-order (permuting adjacent local declarations recolors saved registers and can change the frame), reassociate (permute and parenthesize three-term INTEGER additions -- never floats, that changes results), param-inversion (hoist a call argument into a temp to change evaluation order), bitfield (rewrite a shift+mask extraction into an equivalent form), local-form (introduce a named local for a repeated subexpression), fp-helper (wrap a float expression in (f32)/(f64) to steer f32-vs-double codegen). Two more change semantics and must be checked by hand, never swept blindly: cast (varying s8/u8/char) and width (swapping same-width sign spellings).
note: decl-order is the one to reach for on a regperm or frame-only miss -- it is the only family in this list that moves register colouring and frame layout rather than arithmetic. BANNED here, do not generate: adding volatile locals or volatile byte reads, adding empty switch cases to reshape a jump table, and wrapping snippets in #pragma peephole/scheduling/fp_contract toggles. Those close byte gaps by producing source nobody would write, which the source project rejects outright -- a maintainer review: 'Don't fakematch through manual volatile padding -- leave unmatching, it's ok, we'll figure out real inlines in time.'
tooling: tools/gen-variants.py emits a variants file for the safe families; feed it to tools/try-variants.py and let the measurement decide.
source: Taxonomy observed in 999sian/mwdiff's mutation families (2026-08-24). The tool itself is NOT recommended -- its stated success criterion is 'only exact object measures and a matching linked checksum are success, never a readable decompilation', i.e. it has no readability gate at all. The family list is the only part worth keeping.
diagnosis: tools/structural-diff.py puts the function in the 'length' category with a small delta, or tools/stack-frame-diff.py puts it in 'regperm'.
worked_example: GCConsole2 2026-08-24: six functions sat 1-3 instructions from target with correct frames. processAppearJet needed a bool/compare respelling (&= and direct state mutation instead of a boolean-returning helper), processAppearMario needed explicit break statements, processAppearTank needed two nested threshold conditions combined into one. All six went to 100% with no new logic. Measured 2026-08-24 on startAppearCoin (already matching, frame 0x98): writing a condition as `x != 0` instead of `x` moved the frame to 0xa0 (+8) while keeping the same 316 bytes of code; one compare alias moved it to 0x90 (-8); two other aliases stayed byte-identical. So the bool/compare families are a genuine FRAME lever, not just an arithmetic one -- worth sweeping on a frame-only miss that is off by 8.
